outcomes.text: Understand factual information and abstract ideas in texts about general topics.
Find and select relevant information and details from one or more longer texts.
Identify emotions, opinions and attitudes stated or strongly implied in texts.
Understand arguments and conclusions in discursive texts and distinguish fact from opinion.
Understand texts using both formal and informal language.
Infer the meanings of unfamiliar words from context across various topics.
Understand a broad range of vocabulary used in general topics.
Understand a broad range of language structures, including some complex sentence forms.
Understand lengthy, complex texts and abstract ideas about general and specific topics.
Find and select relevant information and details in longer texts of varied types.
Recognise subtle details, including attitudes and stated or implied opinions.
Understand varied, longer texts written in different styles for different purposes.
Infer unfamiliar words and expressions from context across a wide range of topics.
Understand extensive vocabulary covering general and more specific topics.
Understand a wide range of complex language structures.
Communicate factual information, ideas, opinions and arguments about general topics.
Develop arguments with relevant supporting details and examples.
Write detailed descriptions and narratives of real or imaginary events and experiences.
Organise ideas into coherent paragraphs and longer texts using cohesive devices.
Use register and style appropriate to the text’s purpose and genre.
Use varied vocabulary about general topics accurately.
Use varied grammatical structures, including some complex forms, accurately.
Produce texts demonstrating good control of spelling and punctuation.
Communicate factual information, ideas, opinions and arguments about complex topics.
Develop arguments by evaluating, expanding and supporting viewpoints with reasons and examples.
Write assured, personal and natural descriptions and narratives of real or imaginary experiences.
Organise ideas into fluent, coherent paragraphs using varied cohesive devices.
Use varied vocabulary, including idiom, accurately for general and specific topics.
Use varied complex grammatical structures with a high degree of accuracy.
Produce texts with highly accurate spelling and punctuation.
Read varied literary texts with considerable independence.
Discuss themes, characters, ideas and details while recognising genre conventions.
Develop arguments with relevant supporting details and textual examples.
Give a personal response and explain what is appreciated and why.
Organise ideas into coherent paragraphs and longer responses.
Explain language choices and identify textual features that create reader responses.
Read varied literary texts fluently, appreciating implicit meanings and ideas.
Critically evaluate themes, characters, ideas and details with awareness of genre conventions.
Develop arguments by evaluating important ideas and themes with detailed textual support.
Give a clear personal interpretation and explain reactions to themes and characters.
Organise ideas clearly into coherent paragraphs using appropriate literary terminology.
Analyse language choices and evaluate how they engage the reader.
Understand inclusion, diversity, gender equality and social mobility in society.
Examine ageism, racism and class-based prejudice within society.
Consider immigration, refugee experiences and integration.
Understand social organisation, law and order, governance and communities.
Consider the meaning and responsibilities of national and global citizenship.
Examine individual and governmental rights and responsibilities.
Discuss friendship, family, relationships, generational differences and changing family patterns.
Explore quality of life, living environments, urban-rural differences, overcrowding and social isolation.
Evaluate lifestyle choices involving relationships, diet, fashion, self-expression, values and goals.
Explain global warming, climate change and pollution, including solutions, government action and economic effects.
Consider biodiversity conservation, ecosystem protection and the treatment of animals.
Assess the environmental effects of population growth.
Explore natural-resource use, recycling, waste management and consumerism.
Examine fossil fuels, renewable energy, energy geopolitics and local environmental impacts.
Evaluate ways to reduce environmental impact through housing, food and travel choices.
Understand sustainable tourism and the benefits of travel.
Compare global environmental cooperation with national priorities.
Evaluate the roles of individuals, industry, governments and environmental movements in protecting the planet.
Discuss medical advances and ethical issues in scientific research.
Examine smart technology, privacy and security.
Understand applications and implications of artificial intelligence.
Evaluate the benefits and dangers of digital media.
Understand the role of communication technology.
Explore the development and significance of online communities.
Consider unequal access to technology.
Examine the use of technology in education.
Examine the use of technology in the workplace.
